title: Manufacturing Announcements Can Influence Patentability Challenges: What Quantum Computing Companies Should Know - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Guest legal commentary (the text is bylined Sarah Schlotter and Adam Wichman of Wolf, Greenfield & Sacks) argues that since March 2026 the US Patent Office weighs domestic manufacturing when deciding whether to institute an IPR patent challenge, so quantum companies' CHIPS Act manufacturing announcements may become evidence. The one decision so far, Tesla v. Bulletproof, credited documented, product-specific evidence.

insights.claim: Since March 2026 the US Patent Office treats domestic manufacturing as a factor in whether it will hear a patentability challenge (IPR) against issued patent claims, so a company's description of its manufacturing and funding can affect IPRs it brings or defends.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Patent-dispute outcomes for quantum hardware firms can hinge on how they describe US manufacturing; watch IP risk.

insights.claim: A March 11, 2026 Patent Office Director memorandum named two factors: whether accused products are made in the US or tied to American manufacturing investment, and whether the patent owner's competing products are made in the US.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Defines what evidence parties will be asked to address in IPR proceedings.
insights.locator: Domestic Manufacturing as a Factor to Institute an IPR

insights.claim: Public statements such as press releases about domestic manufacturing may become evidence influencing whether the Patent Office considers a patentability challenge at all.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Treat manufacturing PR as potential legal evidence; review announcements for IP exposure.
insights.quote: A company’s public statements about its domestic manufacturing activities, such as in press releases describing these CHIPS awards, may become evidence

themes.theme: CHIPS Act awards to quantum firms

insights.claim: In September 2026 the Commerce Department finalized CHIPS Act R&D awards of up to $100 million each to several quantum companies including D-Wave, Rigetti, Quantinuum and PsiQuantum to improve manufacturing and domestic supply chains.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Government funding for domestic quantum manufacturing is now finalized; these firms' announcements will also carry patent-legal weight.

insights.claim: In Tesla v. Bulletproof Property Management, the only decision so far applying the manufacturing factors, the Director allowed Tesla's IPR to proceed on unrelated grounds but said Tesla's domestic manufacturing evidence supported the result, crediting six documents including a press release, SEC filing and federal labeling data.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Documented, third-party and government-filed evidence is what counts; a useful guide even though Tesla involved no quantum computing.
insights.locator: The Director’s Decision Applying Domestic Manufacturing Factors

insights.claim: The Director rejected Bulletproof's claim that accused cars contain 30 to 40 percent foreign components because Bulletproof offered no supporting evidence.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Unsupported assertions about foreign content carry no weight; evidence matters on both sides.

insights.claim: Quantum companies should expect their manufacturing announcements to be used as evidence, support each statement with a document, tie manufacturing to specific products via a roadmap, account for components as well as assembly, and keep award documents, supplier agreements and site records.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Checklist for diligence on how quantum firms communicate manufacturing and protect patent positions.

insights.claim: Including partner statements and a hardware roadmap in manufacturing announcements can connect domestic manufacturing investment to specific products that may later be accused of infringement.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Roadmap-linked manufacturing disclosures can strengthen a company's position in later IPR disputes.
insights.locator: What this Means for Quantum Computing Companies
